hook: Supplements probably aren't the answer to your brain fog — because you're trying to solve a downstream problem upstream
topic: Why supplements fail when root mechanisms are unaddressed
body:
**If you've tried supplements for brain fog — and most of them didn't make a meaningful difference — this is why. You were solving a downstream problem upstream.**

Most supplements marketed for cognitive performance operate on neurotransmitter systems or cerebral blood flow. Some have genuine evidence behind them. But their effects are modest when the foundational conditions of brain function are degraded.

You cannot supplement your way out of a glymphatic system that isn't clearing waste because your deep sleep is fragmented. You cannot supplement your way out of blood glucose volatility that is crashing your cognition twice a day. You cannot supplement your way out of chronic cortisol elevation suppressing your prefrontal cortex.

These are structural inputs. Supplements operate downstream of them. Layering a compound on top of an unfixed system is like adding high-quality oil to an engine running at the wrong temperature.

Fix the temperature first. Sleep architecture, glucose stability, hydration, light exposure — these are not the interesting answers, but they are the upstream ones. And upstream is where the fog actually starts.
visual_direction: Dr. Hale slightly more direct and deliberate than usual — this script challenges a behaviour the audience has probably invested money in. The engine analogy lands well visually with a brief split: supplement bottle on one side, the upstream inputs listed on the other.
text_overlay: "Fix the upstream first. Then add downstream."
caption_hook: Tried every supplement and still foggy? You're solving the wrong level of the problem.
